clue.text: You may hold his life in your hands

definitions.text: You may hold his life in your hands

parts.words: You may hold his life in your hands
parts.note: read literally it sounds like holding a person at your mercy; in fact you hold the book in which a writer has set down someone's life story

explanation.definitionFit: A writer of life stories produces a book that a reader holds in their hands.

clue.text: Breeches sometimes put on this lad, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for lad is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is sometimes dressed in breeches.
explanation.walkthrough: A breeches buoy is a canvas seat shaped like trousers, slung on a rope to rescue people from a ship; 'Breeches' looks like clothing for the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeches buoy is a lifebelt with canvas trousers attached, used in sea rescue.

clue.text: Taxing is useless to support an old fiddler

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned
US is crossword shorthand for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A tax on an elderly violinist is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor is said to have fiddled while Rome burned; in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so 'to support' means it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taxing is burdensome and demanding.

clue.text: Rich gravy served in dining cars, for example

parts.note: rolling in it means rich, so rolling is wealthy
stock is the meat broth that gravy is made from

explanation.surface: A rich gravy is served to passengers in the restaurant car of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolling means very rich, as in 'rolling in money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages and wagons collectively make up a line's vehicles, dining cars among them.

clue.text: Line in manuscript under investigation is causing difficulties

indicators.note: in a down clue the manuscript comes under, so after, the investigation
says the line letter goes inside

parts.note: a probe is an investigation

explanation.surface: A line in a manuscript being investigated is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' means placed after; 'in' then slips the line letter into the investigation word.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles or snags that need solving.

clue.text: Alters start of emergency repairs

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of emergency

parts.note: mends means repairs

explanation.surface: Emergency repairs begin to change things.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise a text is to change it.

clue.text: Careful pedestrian? That's a joke!

explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 15, King Agag of the Amalekites came to Samuel 'delicately', which makes him a careful walker; the second half is A plus GAG, 'that's a gag'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical king who walked delicately is the careful walker, and a gag is a joke, so 'that's a gag' covers the exclamation.

clue.text: Stick profit into footwear

parts.note: gum is glue, to gum is to stick
boot is an old word for profit or advantage, kept in 'to boot'

explanation.surface: Someone pockets a profit by stuffing it into their footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Boot as profit survives only in 'to boot', meaning in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber wellington is a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Plucky goalie, Mellors

parts.note: game means brave or willing
a goalkeeper is the keeper

explanation.surface: A brave goalkeeper called Mellors.
explanation.walkthrough: Mellors is the estate worker who is Lady Chatterley's lover in D H Lawrence's novel; the clue makes him a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's Oliver Mellors looks after the birds and game on the Chatterley estate.

clue.text: Some of the bowling was apparently allowed to go unpunished

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, so a portion of the bowling
looked means seemed, that is was apparently

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire let some poor bowling pass without penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket; the surface's cricket picture hides a plain charade of two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore an offence is to let it slide without penalty.

clue.text: It helps to make him a Muslim leader

indicators.note: It helps to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on what qualifies a man as a Muslim leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in hIM A Muslim; 'It helps to make' signals that those words contain it.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who leads prayers in a mosque is a religious head of the congregation.

clue.text: Diet is on course — bodies are tightened up here

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan's Diet
a line is a course, as in a line of action

explanation.surface: A slimmer's diet is on track, and their body is getting toned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' and 'bodies are tightened' suggest slimming, but the diet is a parliament and the bodies are car bodies bolted up in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car factory, vehicle shells are fitted and bolted together along a moving production track.

clue.text: Desert island American sailor found first

indicators.note: says the sailor is placed ahead of the island in the answer

parts.note: gob is US slang for a seaman in the navy

explanation.surface: A desert island where an American sailor was the first to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert island' reads as one phrase, but 'Desert' alone is the definition and 'island' gives I; 'found first' puts GOB before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The great arid region of Mongolia and northern China is a well-known desert.

clue.text: Woman needs overall in the plant

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a smock is a loose overall worn over clothes

explanation.surface: A woman puts on an overall before working among the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuckooflower, a pink meadow wildflower, has this traditional English name.

clue.text: Banter makes one colour in school

indicators.note: says the one and the colour go inside the school

parts.note: the Perse is a well-known independent school in Cambridge
I is the Roman numeral for one
a flag is a colour, as in a regiment's colours

explanation.surface: Light teasing at school turns somebody red.
explanation.walkthrough: The school is the Perse, an independent school in Cambridge, England; 'in' puts one plus the colour inside it. Colours are a regiment's banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, teasing chat or raillery.

clue.text: One readily taken in to child's play?

explanation.definitionFit: A dupe who is easily fooled is a soft target, and a task that needs no effort is a walkover.

clue.text: Motor car project

explanation.definitionFit: Volkswagen's famous rounded car has this name, and to overhang or jut out, as brows do, is to beetle.

clue.text: Feeling one is out for punishment

indicators.note: says the one letter is removed from the feeling word

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The feeling that someone is being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's penalty passed on a convicted person.

clue.text: Put under grave

explanation.definitionFit: To put a patient under with drugs is to tranquillise them, and a grave manner is calm and dignified.

clue.text: Sounds as if janitor by end of shift is asleep

indicators.note: says the word for janitor is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a janitor guards a door, a doorman

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of shift

explanation.surface: A caretaker seems to doze off when the shift ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds as if' gives DOORMAN as heard, DORMAN; 'end of' gives T from shift. 'is' belongs to the definition as an adjective follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive, as in a sleeping state.

clue.text: Padding part of speech, one taking a long time

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
I is the Roman numeral for one
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Wordy filler in a speech, from someone who takes ages to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding in writing is excess wordiness used to fill space.

clue.text: A loss Rosemary should not suffer

definitions.text: A loss Rosemary should not suffer

parts.words: A loss Rosemary should not suffer
parts.note: rosemary is the herb of remembrance, so it of all things should never lose its memory; Rosemary as a name misleads

explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the one thing a herb symbolising remembrance should never undergo.

clue.text: Reddish-brown flying saucer seen in Latin country

indicators.note: says the saucer letters appear inside the country word

parts.note: rus is the Latin word for the country, countryside
a UFO, unidentified flying object

explanation.surface: A rust-coloured flying saucer is spotted over Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin country' suggests Italy or Spain, but it is the Latin word for countryside, RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for a red-brown colour, often used of birds' plumage.

clue.text: Warning by the bench: "You may get tanked up here"

definitions.text: You may get tanked up here

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning that a ball is coming
the bench means the judges, a court of law

explanation.surface: A judge warns a defendant that drunkenness may follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanked up' suggests drink, but it means filled with petrol: the forecourt is where cars are fuelled at a filling station.
explanation.definitionFit: The open area in front of a filling station is where vehicles have their fuel tanks filled.

clue.text: American Name invested in type of cattle

indicators.note: invested means clothed or put inside, so the name letter goes into the cattle word

parts.note: the yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet

explanation.surface: An American name is given to a breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a person from the United States.

clue.text: It's no better than a marsh

explanation.definitionFit: Nothing more than, as in 'only a child'; and an old word for a lake or boggy pool.

clue.text: A hard sailor, the captain

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A tough sailor who rose to command his ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Melville's Moby-Dick is commanded by this obsessive whaling skipper.

clue.text: Meets the children and starts to argue

parts.note: to join is to meet or come together
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Someone meets the children and a quarrel begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up a point of dispute with someone is to begin a disagreement.

clue.text: Food for high teas

indicators.note: high as in gamey or off: the letters of teas have gone bad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something to eat at a high tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high teas' looks like the meal, but 'high' is the anagram signal on 'teas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for things to eat.

clue.text: Solemnly swear to serve at sea in hostilities

indicators.note: in hostilities suggests a battle, turmoil that throws these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A recruit swears an oath to serve at sea during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hostilities' rearranges SERVE AT SEA; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm earnestly, declare positively, as under oath.
